w:r.w:t: EmPay follows a 3-tier Browser/Server (B/S) architecture with a layered MVC pattern on the backend. This is the recommended architecture for web-based HRMS systems per production research (Interact HRMS pattern).
Role-aware UI routing, form handling, chart rendering, state management via Zustand + TanStack Query
JWT auth middleware, RBAC role guard, payroll computation engine, PDF generation, REST API routes
ACID-compliant storage, schema migrations, connection pooling, JSONB audit logs, typed query client
Repository is a monorepo with two root directories. Engineer A owns the backend; Engineer B owns the frontend. This minimizes merge conflicts.
Single source of truth for all DB models and enums
auth.ts (JWT verify), roleGuard.ts (RBAC), errorHandler.ts (global error middleware)
Feature modules: auth/, employees/, attendance/, leaves/, payroll/, analytics/ — each has controller + service + routes
Pure payroll computation function — no DB calls inside; fully unit-testable
Axios instance with base URL + all typed API call functions
Shared UI: Button, Card, Table, Modal, Badge, StatCard, LoadingSpinner
Role-specific page components per module (auth, dashboard, attendance, leaves, payroll, employees)
Zustand store: user object, JWT token, login/logout actions
EmPay uses stateless JWT-based authentication. The role is embedded in the payload to avoid DB round-trips on every request.
Employee UUID — identifies the user for DB lookups
User email — display in UI; never query DB for this
One of: admin | hr_officer | payroll_officer | employee — read in roleGuard middleware
Issued At — auto-set by jsonwebtoken library
Expiry — 8 hours from iat; server rejects expired tokens with HTTP 401
Prevents sequential ID enumeration attacks; safe to expose in API responses
Essential for multi-timezone correctness; IST set as default timezone
Hard delete breaks payslip foreign keys — deactivation preserves data integrity
Exact decimal arithmetic; supports salaries up to ₹9.9 crore/month; no floating point errors
Enforces exactly one attendance record per employee per day at DB level
Prevents duplicate payruns for same period at DB level
Flexible schema for any entity mutation; queryable with PostgreSQL JSON operators
users 1:1 employee_profiles (each user has one profile)
users 1:N leave_requests (employee may have many requests)
users 1:N leave_balances (one per leave type per year)
payroll_runs 1:N payslips (one payslip per employee per run)
audit_logs N:1 users (each log entry references an actor)
Pure function: payrollEngine.ts takes inputs, returns outputs, makes zero DB calls
All data pre-fetched in the payrun controller before calling the engine
Engine wrapped in a Prisma transaction: if any payslip write fails, all are rolled back
Deterministic: same employee + same month data always produces the same payslip
Controller fetches: salary_structures, attendance records, approved leave_requests for the month
attendanceSummary computed: workingDays (22), presentDays, unpaidAbsences (absent + unpaid leave days)
payrollEngine.computePayslip(employee, salaryStructure, attendanceSummary) called per employee
Payslip object returned and bulk-inserted via Prisma transaction
Vite build artifact deployed; VITE_API_URL env var points to Railway backend URL; preview URLs per branch
Node.js service; PORT auto-assigned; DATABASE_URL and JWT_SECRET set as env vars; health check endpoint /api/health
DATABASE_URL auto-injected; connection_limit=5 set in Prisma datasource URL; pgbouncer if available
ALLOWED_ORIGIN env var set to exact Vercel domain; configured from Hour 0 to prevent prod CORS failures
